page: Amazon Web Services m7i.12xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores, utilizing the Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The system includes 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are included in this configuration, and network connectivity is established with a 19 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). These hardware capabilities are reflected in strong benchmark results, with the server placing in the top 25% for Passmark CPU scores, extended instructions, and encryption tests. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng performance benchmarks fall within the average range.

Memory performance is characterized by strong read-only bandwidth for small cached blocks, though large block read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier. The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. Additionally, the AMX instructions contribute to strong LLM inference speeds, achieving top-tier performance for text generation with small models and strong performance for medium models.

The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads. However, the balanced compute-to-memory ratio and strong cryptographic and vector instruction support make this server suitable for database operations, web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
